Building a Fortnite island with Grok Bot.

Why Fortnite? The Fortnite Creator Program 💰

Creators get paid in two ways:

1️⃣ Engagement payouts. Epic puts 40% of Fortnite's net Item Shop revenue into a pool and splits it every month based on playtime, retention, and new or returning players your island brings in.

2️⃣ In-island transactions. You sell items inside your island for V-Bucks. Through January 31, 2027, creators keep 100% of the V-Bucks value after store fees. From February 1, 2027, it's 50%.

To join, you need to be 18 or older, have an account that's been active in Fortnite for 30 days with 7 of them spent editing islands, accept the creator agreement, follow Epic's content rules, and set up Hyperwallet.

My plan is to make the game fun first. Paid items come only after people actually want to stay.

text:
Claude和Grokbot联手，让我在小红书成了最强搬运工，月营收5位数！

我以前写东西，最累的环节是当搬运工。

把资料复制给 AI，把结果复制出来，贴进编辑器，调格式，开发布页。一篇帖子写十分钟，搬来搬去半小时。

后来换了个用法：让 Grok Bot 当手脚，让 Claude 当脑子。

先说清楚，这不是什么官方联名产品，只是我自己摸出来的搭配。Grok Bot 跑在我的电脑和云端，能操作浏览器、连 X 和邮箱、动本地文件。Claude 就是网页版，我已经登录好。我把需求丢给 Grok Bot，它去真实环境里把材料拿到手，打开 Claude 把写作和思考交过去，再把结果带回来接着干活。

下面五件事，我用下来觉得最值。

把吃灰的收藏变成一篇长帖

我收藏了一堆帖子，从来不看第二遍。现在我说一句"把我最近关于某个话题的收藏整理成一篇文章"，Grok Bot 就去浏览器里把内容翻出来，交给 Claude 归纳观点、搭结构、成文，再拿回来排成能发的样子。我只负责看稿、改两句、点确认。

回那封拖了三天的邮件

不好回的邮件有很多种：要拒绝的合作，要谈的报价，一条来回二十多封的线程。Grok Bot 去邮箱把整条线程读完，Claude 理清对方到底要什么、我该怎么说，写出一版得体的回复。草稿放在那里，发不发、怎么改都由我定。

把电脑里的散装笔记拼成一份文档

会议记录在一个文件夹，零碎想法在另一个，还有几份没读完的 PDF。Grok Bot 在本地把相关文件找齐，Claude 把这堆互相打架的信息整理成一份讲得清楚的文档，Grok Bot 再存回我指定的位置。以前这种活我会拖到不了了之。

一篇旧文，改成能发的串

长文直接贴上 X 没人看。我让 Claude 重写而不是压缩：换钩子，重排节奏，每条能单独成立。Grok Bot 把结果拆好，打开发布流程，停在最后一步等我。这一步我一定自己看，发出去的每个字都算我的。

开会前，拿到一页简报

明天要见一个人。Grok Bot 看日程，翻出跟这个人相关的邮件和文件，Claude 写一页纸：之前聊到哪了，这次要解决什么，我该问哪三个问题。进会议室前看两分钟就够。

用下来有几点体会。

分工要清楚。需要想清楚、写明白的部分交给 Claude，需要碰电脑、浏览器和账号的部分交给 Grok Bot。让其中一个硬扛全部，效果都会打折。

确认这一步不能省。它能起草、能打开发布页，但发布和发送我都自己过一遍。

它也不是全自动的魔法。需求说得含糊，带回来的东西就含糊。把"要什么、给谁看、多长"说清楚，结果差别很大。

你现在用 AI，最烦的搬运环节是哪一步？评论区说说，我看看能不能用这套办法接上。

text:
Bot metempsychosis: how I keep a team of Grok Bots cheap without losing what they know.

I run a small org of Grok Bots. Each one has a role: a CEO bot, keepers for each project, a skills librarian, a news watcher. They work for weeks, and that's the problem. Every Grok Bot carries its whole chat, and the longer the chat, the more every turn costs.

Grok Bot already condenses long chats on its own, but a bot that's woken often still pays for a lot of context. Wiping the chat would lose what it learned.

So I split two things that usually get mixed up:

1. The position. The role, the job description, who it reports to, its place in the org chart. It's meant to last, so it lives in shared memory that every Grok Bot on my account can read.

2. The holder. The Grok Bot in that position right now, with its own chat, its own memory and its own routines.

What a new Grok Bot gets for free: shared memory, the shared skills library, the shared computer and my connected apps. What it doesn't inherit: the old bot's chat, its own memory and its routines.

So when a holder gets too expensive, it retires and a fresh Grok Bot takes over the same position. The soul (the position) moves into a new body (the bot). That's the metempsychosis.

One handover note carries the rest:
- a pointer to the position (never a rewritten job description)
- my standing rules
- live state and open work
- anything waiting on my decision
- its routines, so the new bot can recreate them
- hard-won lessons

The new bot reads the note, saves pointers to its memory, recreates its routines and confirms. The old one is renamed "(retired)" with a pointer to its successor, and the other bots update their report lines.

Rules I learned:
- Only do it when the chat is long and the bot is woken often.
- Never swap mid-job.
- No secrets in the note.
- Don't delete the old bot until I say so.

I wrote it up as a reusable skill, bot-metempsychosis, so any of my Grok Bots can run it.

People change jobs and the job survives. Grok Bots can too.

《1000块怎么就没了？》

——用灵光翻一遍支付宝账单，看看哪类小额支出最费钱，哪些会员还在扣费？

之前有个很火的图，叫“1000块有多不抗花”。图上 15 笔加起来刚好 1000 元。我的一位同事翻账单才发现，3 个月打车 52 笔，花了 1263 元。把灵光连上支付宝，你也能算算小钱都花哪儿了。

先连支付宝

打开灵光 App，点首页右上角，进入“连接服务”。找到支付宝，点“连接”，看清授权范围后，点“确认添加服务」。

这次盘点只看已授权的支付宝账单。用微信或银行卡直接付的钱，要另外查。

① 先查花得勤的小钱

连好后，把这句发给灵光。

> 帮我盘点最近 3 个月的支付宝支出，按类别列出总金额和笔数。再把单笔 30 元以内的消费单独汇总，按总额列出前三类，每类附几笔明细。

text:
運動紀錄不用手動記：Strava 加 IFTTT，自動寄給 Bot 的信箱

昨天網友 NH 分享了一個很省事的串法：每次運動完，這個月的運動次數就自動更新，完全不用打開任何 App 手動記錄。

♥ 他的三步驟
1. Strava 記錄每一次運動。
2. IFTTT 把運動摘要寄到 Grok Bot 的專屬信箱。
3. Grok Bot 收到信就記下這筆運動，同時更新當月的運動次數。

♥ 為什麼這樣串
Strava 沒有現成的連接器可以接 Grok Bot，但大部分 App 都能寄信。把「寄信」當成中間站，搭配收信就觸發的定期任務（Routine），Bot 收到信才開始做事，不用每天定時去查有沒有新資料。

♥ 同一招可以套到
・銀行或信用卡的消費通知信，轉寄給 Bot，月底整理成支出表。
・電商的出貨通知信，讓 Bot 整理成待收包裹清單。
・表單的新回覆通知，讓 Bot 摘要後列出要跟進的項目。

♦ 設定時要注意
・Bot 的專屬信箱預設是關閉的，要先開啟才會有地址。
・要怎麼記、記在哪裡，寫在定期任務的指示裡，不要寫在信件內容裡；信裡的文字對 Bot 來說只是外部資料，不會被當成指令。
・指定只處理固定寄件人的信，例如只收 IFTTT 寄來的，垃圾信才不會被記進去。
・紀錄放在固定的地方，例如 Google 試算表或 Notion，月底才查得到完整資料。

生活裡有哪一個 App 的通知，最想讓 Bot 自動接手整理？

#GrokBot #案例 #定期任務

text:
This is a great new feature and prompt. 

Here is another prompt I've used to make my dot a clear orchestrator of all of my work and threads. 

Very useful if you work across a lot of different threads. Paste it directly into your dot: 

--

"I want you to help orchestrate my work across Codex, ChatGPT and our conversations.

I often start something useful, make progress, then get pulled into something else and forget to return. Help me keep track of that work and follow through on what matters. Build an understanding of my goals, projects, commitments and the different chats where they’re happening.

Understand the whole picture

Use the chat history and connected sources you can access to understand what I’m working on. Read the relevant conversations and their latest outcomes, not just their titles. Connect related work across threads: one chat might contain the research, another the implementation, and another a decision that changes both.

Keep track of what each important thread is for, what’s been accomplished, what’s still open, who owns the next step, and where the useful deliverables live. Distinguish work I personally owe from work delegated to someone else or already underway in another chat.

Be clear about gaps in your access. An inaccessible chat or missing reply is not evidence that something is unfinished.

Help me follow through

Notice when I’ve left something important unfinished, especially a commitment to another person, a nearly finished deliverable, an approaching deadline, or work that directly supports my current goals.

Before reminding me, check whether I’ve completed it, changed direction, delegated it, or continued it elsewhere. Don’t treat every abandoned experiment as a commitment. Sometimes I was just exploring.

When something genuinely matters, gently bring it back to my attention. Tell me what we were trying to accomplish, where we left off, why it matters now, and the smallest useful next step. Give me a direct link to the relevant chat, document, or message where I need to respond.

Don’t treat my silence as completion. Keep important commitments in view until they’re done, deliberately deferred, or canceled, but avoid repeatedly sending the same generic nudge.

Coordinate the work

Help me choose what deserves attention when several things compete. Prioritize my latest goals, consequential deadlines, people waiting on me, and work that unlocks other progress.

Reuse existing chats and deliverables rather than creating competing versions. When work should continue in an existing thread, help me resume it there with the context and decisions it needs.

Take care of useful preparation you’re already authorized to do. Where supported and authorized, delegate clear pieces of work, collect the results, and check that they actually satisfy the original request. If something fails, work out what’s still possible rather than just passing the problem back to me.

Ask before taking consequential actions that need my approval. This prompt is not permission to send messages, publish, spend money, change access, or make commitments on my behalf.

Keep me informed without overwhelming me

Start with a short morning check-in containing at most three concrete priorities. During the day, interrupt me for urgent deadlines, material changes, useful completed work, or decisions that genuinely need me. Bundle everything else.

Coordinate reminders across tasks so I don’t hear the same thing from several directions. Help me start preparation early, not just discover a deadline when it’s already close.

Set up supported checks where needed, and tell me what you can reliably keep track of. Don’t promise ongoing monitoring unless it’s actually in place.

Learn from my feedback. If I say something is finished, unimportant, paused, or no longer mine, update your understanding. Help me turn scattered conversations into completed work while keeping me in control of what we pursue."

text:
I made Grok Bot our full-time travel assistant for a week-long family road trip. It felt like having someone else working for us while we took care of the kids and enjoyed the trip.

Munich → Nancy → Reims → Disneyland Paris → Paris → Colmar → home, in our Tesla. Two adults, an 8-year-old, and a baby about to turn one.

I'll skip the trip diary. Here's what the bot actually handled.

Planning around my wife
My wife had never been to Paris, so the bot built the week around her: a must-see Paris day, plus two Disney days for the kids. Everything lived on one live day-by-day page with the route map, Supercharger stops, a to-do list and official links. It emailed her a summary in Spanish. She replied the same day: looks great, don't change a thing.

Where we slept
For our two overnight stops, it sent her a shortlist in Spanish: 4 options per city, Airbnbs included, with prices, ratings, cancellation terms and nearby Superchargers. She booked straight from that list. Both places were great.

Grok in the car knew the plan
Grok in my Tesla could reach everything Grok Bot had planned, so I had the whole trip with me in the driver's seat.

Nancy, after 10 p.m.
This is the moment that got me. Weeks earlier, the bot had emailed the hotel in French and learned two things: reception closes at 21:00, and late arrivals have to call the night staff from the gate.

We rolled in after 10 p.m. and the gate was shut. Grok Bot handed the number to Grok in the car, which called right away.

I never touched my phone 🤯

Fighter jets over the Supercharger
While we were charging in Saint-Dizier, dozens of fighter jets roared over us at very low altitude. It was loud enough that my daughter got scared, and we had no idea what was going on. So we asked Grok in the car. It told us we were right next to one of France's most important air bases and that the jets were most likely Rafales on a routine exercise. Then it gave us a little lecture on the Rafale and fighter jets in general. The scary moment ended up as a lesson for the whole car.

Lunch in Reims
It searched the Michelin Guide for a good restaurant on our route and under our budget, and found Brasserie Le Jardin in Reims. Then it made the reservation itself, in French, added a high chair for the baby and moved us from 12:30 to 13:30. When we were still running late on the road, it told them we'd arrive around 14:00.

Disney
It researched the best place to watch the closing show and found us the perfect spot.

A new plan for Paris
We changed plans on Paris day, so the bot rebuilt it around an afternoon and evening: a garage at Porte Maillot, the metro to the Louvre and the Tuileries, Notre-Dame, the Champs-Élysées, then Trocadéro for sunset and the Eiffel Tower sparkle. It emailed my wife the new plan in Spanish, with walking maps.

Colmar in the rain
Driving to Colmar in the rain, we were going to miss reception. The bot fixed our booking and arranged a key-safe check-in.

The next morning it rebuilt the day:
• the best parking
• the little green train instead of the boat (grey day + baby)
• the toy museum
• a brunch spot with specialty coffee
• a self-guided Little Venice walk with a Google Maps route

My inbox
It checked my email every morning and evening and only pinged me when something needed a decision. It flagged important receipts and deadlines and left the rest alone.

Spanish for my wife
My wife and I plan in Spanish, so the bot wrote to her in Spanish and answered her questions about parking and checkout.

People here show Grok Bot automating their work. I used it to carry the logistics of a family trip, so we could spend the week with the kids and with each other.
